title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). 𝔖 is a profinite group with an index-2 subgroup 𝔖⁺ = Ĝ⁺, and ε_𝔖 : 𝔖 → 𝔖/𝔖⁺ ≅ {±1} is the sign character. ρ and σ are distinguished elements, apparently torsion elements, which topologically generate 𝔖⁺. The elements ε₀ and ε₁ (with ε₁^{μ-1} = ρ₁^ν, ν = (μ-1)/2) are attached to the subgroups L₀ and L₁. The probable model is a profinite completion of a modular-type group (SL₂(Z)/PSL₂(Z), M_{1,1}, or the M_{0,4} picture), with 𝔖⁺ the orientation-preserving part. The 'équation des lacets' is the profinite equation that cuts out Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type automorphisms.

The previous page defines Σ_{ρ,σ} as the set of tuples (ξ, η, μ, ε', ε) with ξ, η ∈ 𝔖⁺, μ ∈ Ẑ*, ε', ε = ±1, such that:
- ξρ is 𝔖⁺-conjugate to ρ^{ε'};
- ησ is 𝔖⁺-conjugate to σ^ε;
- ξ = η ε₁^{μ-1}.
It also defines SG_{ρ,σ} as the set of triples (α, β, μ) ∈ 𝔖 × 𝔖 × Ẑ* with [α,ρ] = [β,σ] ε₁^{μ-1}. The map (71) sends (α, β, μ) to ([α,ρ], [β,σ], μ, ε_𝔖(α), ε_𝔖(β)), and is surjective.

This page does four things.
- (72) defines the 'effective' part Σ^{eff} ⊂ Σ. It consists of the tuples realised by an automorphism u ∈ Aut(Ĝ⁺) with u(ρ) = ξρ and u(σ) = ησ, i.e. [u,ρ] = ξ and [u,σ] = η. Such a u is unique because ρ and σ generate Ĝ⁺. The page then notes that Σ^{eff} is in bijection with the systems (u, μ, ε', ε) satisfying: u(ρ) is conjugate to ρ^{ε'}; u(σ) is conjugate to σ^ε; u(ε₀) = ε₀^μ. The last condition is the translation of ξ = η ε₁^{μ-1}.
- These systems form a subgroup B_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(Ĝ⁺) × Ẑ* × {±1} × {±1}, defined earlier (p. 577'). This gives the bijection (73), u ↦ ([u,ρ], [u,σ], χ(u), ε'(u), ε(u)). In other words, Σ^{eff} is the 'orbit' of the group B: a GT-like group of automorphisms that preserve the conjugacy classes of the generators up to inversion and act on ε₀ through a cyclotomic-type character χ.
- (74) defines SG^{eff} as the inverse image of Σ^{eff} under (71). Concretely, these are the triples (α, β, μ) satisfying the loop equation [α,ρ] = [β,σ] ε₁^{μ-1} for which the assignment ρ ↦ αρα⁻¹, σ ↦ βσβ⁻¹ extends to an automorphism u of Ĝ⁺.
- (75) records the induced surjection SG^{eff} → Σ^{eff}.

The next page compares SG^{eff} with a fibre product built from B and the normalisers N_ρ*, N_σ*, and proves that comparison map is injective. The purpose is to parametrise the automorphism group (a GT-analogue) by solutions (α, β, μ) of the 'loop equation', modulo centralisers Z_ρ and Z_σ. This is the analogue of describing GT elements by pairs (λ, f) with x ↦ x^λ, y ↦ f⁻¹ y^λ f, here with exponent (λ-1)/2 as in Drinfeld's hexagon.
errors: The ambient set in (74) is written as Ĝ⁺ × Ĝ⁺ × Ẑ* (or ambiguously 𝔖'), but by (70) α and β live in 𝔖 (they may have sign -1). It should read 𝔖 × 𝔖 × Ẑ*. This is a minor slip.
The notation is overloaded. [u,ρ] means u(ρ)ρ⁻¹ when u is an automorphism, and αρα⁻¹ρ⁻¹ when α is a group element; α(ρ) means conjugation by α. This is consistent but implicit.

The uniqueness of u, and the claim that the systems (u, μ, ε', ε) form a group, tacitly use that ρ and σ topologically generate Ĝ⁺ and that μ, ε', ε are functions of u. That is fine but unstated here.

ideas.what: Parametrising automorphisms of a profinite group generated by two torsion-type elements via conjugators (α, β) satisfying a 'loop equation' [α,ρ] = [β,σ] ε₁^{μ-1}, with exponent ν = (μ-1)/2
ideas.modern_name: Drinfeld-type parametrisation of GT elements by (λ, f) and the hexagon-type relation; GT acting on profinite SL₂(Z)/M_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; for the modular-group version Lochak–Schneps, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1997)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the Teichmüller tower and GT programme, but not this explicit equation

ideas.what: Effective subset Σ^{eff}: the solutions of the loop equation that come from genuine automorphisms, identified via a bijection with a group B_{ρ,σ} of automorphisms preserving the conjugacy classes of ρ and σ up to sign
ideas.modern_name: Image of a GT-type group in Out/Aut of the profinite modular group; inertia-preserving automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura, and later Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki for inertia-preserving automorphism groups

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the 'effective' versus 'formal' solution sets for the loop equation and a fibre-product description (continued on the next page) in which the solutions are fibred over a GT-type group with fibres given by normalisers/centralisers. It is a careful bookkeeping of the gap between formal solutions of the equation and actual automorphisms. Nothing on this page appears to go beyond what later GT literature handles, but it documents his independent route to a GT-analogue for a modular-type group.
missed.quote: or cet ensemble n'est autre que le sous-groupe B_{ρ,σ} de Aut(G⁺)×Ẑ*×{±1}×{±1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows Grothendieck explicitly comparing solutions of the loop equation with automorphism groups, a question (do all formal solutions come from automorphisms?) studied later in work on GT versus Aut of profinite modular and braid groups.

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful set-theoretic bookkeeping steps (the effective subset, a bijection with a group, an inverse image) within his GT-like analysis. The ideas are of independent historical interest, but the content of this page is routine and parallels later GT work.
transcription_corrections: The superscript on Σ and SG is most likely 'eff' (effectif), not 'ét'; the next page reads SG^{eff}.
The condition in (72) should read 'et induisant le caractère μ de Ẑ* sur ξ,η' (unclear), i.e. u(ε₀) = ε₀^μ.
In (74) the ambient set is better read as 𝔖 × 𝔖 × Ẑ* (consistent with (70)).
Read 'u(ρ) = α(ρ)' as the image of ρ under conjugation by α.
Read 'une homomorphisme surjectif' as an application surjective induite par (71); the word is uncertain.
